title: The Song Of Moses & The Song Of The Lamb

sense.text:
Keep the picture of the fall of the Moors on the screen and read it: “And it was given unto him to make war with the saints”. Stress the word him: “it was given unto him”. That makes a big difference, because that him is the white man. They made war with the saints, and we are the saints, the children of Israel. They made war with us.

“And to overcome them”: look at the picture, they overcame us. This is war. The Moors, and the word Moor simply means blacks, were Israelites who ruled Europe for close to a thousand years, and it was the white man, Esau’s people, the nation of Esau, that came to fight against us, and at the end of the day they did conquer us, which was according to Bible prophecy. That was the beginning of how they began to conquer and enslave us. You see the lion of Judah on the shield of the last Moor, and you see them chopping us up, murdering us, assassinating us. All the movies of whites besieging each other are false; this is the true ancient history.

“And power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations”: power was given unto the white men over all kindreds, tongues and nations. The eagles on their shield, the birds with two heads, cover the East and the West.

“And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth”: the four corners of the earth are the north, south, east and west. “Holding the four winds of the earth”: the four winds are destruction, military, war. The angels hold them back “that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.”

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”. The seal of the living God is the law. He cries “to the four angels, to whom it was given to hurt the earth and the sea”.

“Saying, Hurt not the earth”, meaning don’t bring destruction yet; “neither the sea”, neither your navy on the sea; “nor the trees”, don’t destroy them, “till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” That is what is holding back the inevitability of Armageddon: the sealing of the saints.

“And I heard the number of them which were sealed”: “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Bible prophecy is being fulfilled, and you men need to really understand you’re all a part of this. We’re all a part of this.

Twelve thousand sealed of every tribe, Juda, Reuben, Gad, Aser, Nepthalim, Manasses, Simeon, Levi, Issachar, Zabulon, Joseph and Benjamin. Verses 5 through 8 are the leading men, the leaders of the nation. People always ask why it says Joseph: when it says Joseph it is referring to Ephraim.

“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands”. This great multitude are Israelites: men, women and children, Israelites coming out of all these places.

Christians try to get you on the street with this verse: Revelation 7:9 says all nations, kindreds, tongues and peoples. It ain’t talking about Chinese and Japanese. It is Israelites coming from all those various lands, the nations they were scattered among. All you men that teach, and you women that teach your kids, need to understand this so they don’t be teaching dumb, stupid Christian stuff.
“And cried with a loud voice, saying, Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb.” That loud cry is the great multitude of Israel.

precepts.why: The proof that the four winds are the military: “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven”. A multitude of men gathered from the four winds: those are the armies. So when the four angels hold the four winds of the earth in Revelation 7:1, they are holding back war and destruction.

“Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” Seal what? The law. The seal of the living God that the angel carries out of the east is the law.

It is sealed “among my disciples”, and the word disciples means students. We are all disciples of Christ; we’re all students.

People always ask why the list of tribes says Joseph. Write this down: “Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions”.

Then verse 19: “Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim”. The stick of Joseph is in the hand of Ephraim. So when Revelation 7:8 says the tribe of Joseph, it is referring to Ephraim.

Who is the great multitude? “Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth”.

The Most High gathers his own seed, his sons and his daughters, out of every direction of the earth. That is the multitude of Revelation 7:9: Israelite men, women and children gathered out of all the lands.

This is the better scripture to use to prove what Revelation 7:9 is talking about: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”. The children of Israel are the ones who cannot be measured nor numbered; that is the multitude “which no man could number”. This is what Revelation 7:9 is saying.

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people”, that’s here in America, “there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.” So this great multitude which cannot be measured or numbered are the children of Israel.

Another precept; write these down. “Thus saith the Lord God; When I shall have gathered the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered”. Stress “from the people”: Israel is scattered among the people, among the nations. That is why the multitude comes “of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues”. It is Israel being gathered out of them.

“And shall be sanctified in them in the sight of the heathen, then shall they dwell in their land that I have given to my servant”.

Another precept for Revelation 7:9, for when Christians try to get you on the street and say Revelation 7:9 means all nations, kindreds, tongues and peoples: “I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs.”

This great people, whom he could not number, is on what mount? Mount Sion. Mount Zion is another name for the twelve tribes of Israel. So it ain’t talking about Chinese and Japanese and everybody. It is Israelites coming from all those various lands, praising the Lord with songs before the throne.

sense.text: “And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvellous, seven angels having the seven last plagues”: destruction. “For in them is filled up the wrath of God”, and the wrath of God is destruction.

“And I saw as it were a sea of glass mingled with fire”: this sea of glass mingled with fire is destruction.

“And them that had gotten the victory over the beast”: that beast is the white man. The seven-headed beast is Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia and Great Britain, and out of the eighth, America came out of Britain. The Lord is saying we got the victory over them.

“And over his image”: the image he portrays throughout the earth. The original of the bust they call Christ was found in a church that is now destroyed, and it is ‘an open secret’ that the son of Pope Alexander posed for it. What’s always funny is that phrase, an open secret. Our people didn’t know about it. So who was it open to? White folks. They always knew that that was not Jesus Christ. Its name is the word for savior; that’s the one your mothers and fathers pray to, that they do the sign of the cross to when they pass, and this is the image some of them will kill you for if you disrespect it. Leonardo da Vinci made sketches of that same man as Christ. It was an open secret, and now it’s open to us.

“And over his mark”: the mark is sin. “And over the number of his name”: the number of his name is 666, which is a number of destruction; that’s what it means. They “stand on the sea of glass, having the harps of God.”

“And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb”. This is what we wanted to get to. What are they going to say? “Saying, Great and marvellous are thy works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are thy ways, thou King of saints.”

So what is the song of Moses? Revelation 15 only gives a brief description, a glory hallelujah of a song. The detail of the song is in Deuteronomy 31.

precepts.why: His mark: “If I sin, then thou markest me”. The mark is sin. Job 10:14 is quick on the street when you’re teaching people, because there’s always somebody on the side saying the mark is a microchip. We’re not saying run around and put microchips in your body; don’t do that. But the mark is sin, and those standing on the sea of glass got the victory over it.

“And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet colour”: that woman represents the United States of America, the Statue of Liberty that sits in the bay. “And decked with gold and precious stones and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand full of abominations and filthiness of her fornication”. What’s in the cup? Abominations. This is sin.

Now the next verse: “And upon her forehead”. First it was the cup in her hand, now her forehead, meaning in her mind, “was a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT”. Babylon the great is the United States of America. “The mother of harlots”: she’s the mother of harlots. “And abominations of the earth”, abominations plural. It’s all sin, brothers and sisters, a sinful system promoting sin.

Now they’re trying to make a way for pedophilia. They don’t call it pedophilia; they call it MAP, meaning you’re attracted to a minor. These people are wicked as hell. That is the mark and the beast system Israel gets the victory over.

sense.text: “And the Lord said unto Moses, Behold, thou shalt sleep with thy fathers; and this people will rise up, and go a whoring after the gods of the strangers of the land”. Imagine this: the Lord is telling Moses, you’re going to die. Your physical body is going to die, and after your body is dead your people, the children of Israel, will rise up and go a whoring after other gods. Moses was not afraid to die. What was going on in his head? Nothing. He was chill, he was at peace, because he understood.

“Then my anger shall be kindled against them in that day, and I will forsake them, and I will hide my face from them, and they shall be devoured, and many evils and troubles shall befall them; so that they will say in that day, Are not these evils come upon us, because our God is not among us?” We’re in those days, even to now, from the time after 70 AD on up.

“And I will surely hide my face in that day for all the evils which they shall have wrought”. That also includes when we went into the Assyrian captivity, Babylonian, Persian, Mede, Greek and Roman, and after that the United States of America, Britain and Spain. “In that they are turned unto other gods”: he ain’t answering our prayers because we are praying to other gods.

“Now therefore write ye this song for you”. He said write this song, “and teach it the children of Israel”. He wanted us to learn this song; this is the song of Moses. “Put it in their mouths, that this song may be a witness for me against the children of Israel.”

“For when I shall have brought them into the land which I sware unto their fathers, that floweth with milk and honey; and they shall have eaten and filled themselves, and waxen fat; then will they turn unto other gods, and serve them, and provoke me, and break my covenant.” He’s telling Moses in this song that the twelve tribes are going to enter the promised land, and once they enter the promised land and grow fat, meaning rich and wealthy, they’re going to turn against him and break his covenant.

“And it shall come to pass, when many evils and troubles are befallen them, that this song shall testify against them as a witness; for it shall not be forgotten out of the mouths of their seed: for I know their imagination which they go about, even now, before I have brought them into the land which I sware.” Even now, because our people were rebellious in the wilderness.
“Moses therefore wrote this song the same day, and taught it the children of Israel.”

“Gather unto me all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, that I may speak these words in their ears, and call heaven and earth to record against them. For I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves”. Moses is now telling us what God told him in the mount: “and turn aside from the way which I have commanded you; and evil will befall you in the latter days”. What days? The latter days. That’s today. “Because ye will do evil in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger through the work of your hands.”
“And Moses spake in the ears of all the congregation of Israel the words of this song, until they were ended.” And the song continues into chapter 32.
The song of Moses: “Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth.”

“My doctrine shall drop as the rain”. God’s doctrine is the law. “My speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass”: meaning his law is going to cover the entire planet earth. That ain’t come yet; that has not happened yet.
“Because I will publish the name of the Lord: ascribe ye greatness unto our God.”
“He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.” That rock is Christ.

“They have corrupted themselves, their spot is not the spot of his children”, because sin corrupts you. It is prophesying what would happen to us. Meaning what? We would forsake the law. And that’s what was said about marriage: having neither spot nor wrinkle in your marriage. Their spot is not the spot of his children because we want to act like the other nations: I can get a divorce from you and take half of all you got, I don’t have to work a day in my life, I’ll get alimony the rest of my life. Those out there who keep doing that for no reason do it because they’re evil, and the Lord is going to deal with them. If it ain’t you, let it roll off your back. But if it’s you, you had a good man and you decided to divorce him, take half and live the life of Riley, then I’m talking about you. This is why a lot of black men say they’re not getting married.

“They are a perverse and crooked generation.” We’ve become perverse and crooked in our lifestyles, and you thought it was normal.

precepts.why: So the doctrine: “For I give you good doctrine, forsake ye not my law.” What’s God’s doctrine, brothers? The law. So when the song says “My doctrine shall drop as the rain”, it is the law of the Most High that will come down and cover the whole earth.

“And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea; and did all eat the same spiritual meat; and did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.”

So when Moses sings “He is the Rock, his work is perfect”, the Rock is Christ, the one who followed Israel through the wilderness.

“The God of my rock; in him will I trust: he is my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge, my saviour; thou savest me from violence.” The Rock of Deuteronomy 32:4 is our shield, our salvation, our high tower, our refuge and our saviour.

The precept about marriage that speaks of spot: “That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.” He is talking about the nation of Israel, the true nation of Israel, not having spot or wrinkle. So when the song says “their spot is not the spot of his children”, it means we forsook the law, and that is the spot and wrinkle his children are not to have.

He is talking about marriage in the context: “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh. This is a great mystery”. Marriage is a great mystery; most brothers and a lot of sisters don’t understand marriage. What does it symbolize? “But I speak concerning Christ and the church.” That’s what marriage symbolizes.

If black men and black women understood that, there would be no divorce. There is divorce because you don’t understand what you’re getting into. Everybody wants to get married, but you don’t understand what it’s about.

Eve came from the side of who? Adam. “Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular.” We read that and just take it for granted, but it means the elect Israelites are members of Christ’s body. That’s what marriage is about. When Christ created the Israelites, we are parts of him; we are part of him. We’re not like the other nations. When God created Adam he took Eve from his side, and we came from Christ’s side. That’s another level right there.

So when the black woman goes and takes up with a white man, she’s destroying herself. That is the spot that is not the spot of his children.

You think this is normal? “Against whom do ye sport yourselves? against whom make ye a wide mouth, and draw out the tongue?” This is what the Bible is talking about; look at what is put on album covers today. He said you’re a perverse, you’re a crooked generation. You didn’t know that was in the Bible, did you?

“Are ye not children of transgression, a seed of falsehood”. That is the perverse and crooked generation of Deuteronomy 32:5.

sense.text: “Do ye thus requite the Lord”: the word requite means revenge. “O foolish people and unwise”: he’s calling us foolish and unwise.
“Remember the days of old”: he’s saying, bethink yourselves, remember the days of old, “consider the years of many generations”.

“When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel”: that means we got the best of the lands, because we’re his chosen.

He separated the sons of Adam. He never wanted them to co-mingle, cohabitate; that was always against his law. Y’all see white folks on the news saying nobody is marrying my white daughter, and y’all be getting mad. What you mad for? That’s Bible. ‘Did not Solomon sin by these things?’
“For the Lord’s portion is his people”: meaning we’re his chosen, “Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.”

precepts.why: What does it mean, the Lord’s portion is his people? “Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen”. We are the chosen people of God, and nobody else. We are the chosen.

sense.text: “He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about”: this is when we were in the wilderness. Moses is going through the history. “He instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye”: his fervent lover.

“As an eagle stirreth up her nest, fluttereth over her young, spreadeth abroad her wings, taketh them, beareth them on her wings”: he’s still talking about what happened in Egypt. From here Moses goes into the history of us being in the wilderness after Egypt.
“So the Lord alone did lead him, and there was no strange god with him”: we weren’t worshipping strange gods.

“He made him ride on the high places of the earth, that he might eat the increase of the fields”: we got the best. “And he made him to suck honey out of the rock, and oil out of the flinty rock”: meaning we got the best of all things when we got into the promised land, “Butter of kine, and milk of sheep, with fat of lambs, and rams of the breed of Bashan” and “the pure blood of the grape.”

precepts.why: The wilderness he found us in: “Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget the Lord thy God, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage; Who led thee through that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents, and scorpions, and drought, where there was no water; who brought thee forth water out of the rock of flint”. That great and terrible wilderness is the “waste howling wilderness” of the song.
The apple of his eye: “Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings”.

“Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Babylon is Esau, the United States of America; we dwell with them.

“After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you”: all the nations spoiled us, they robbed us, they enslaved us. “For he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye”: he that touches us, Mount Zion, the Israelites, touches the apple of his eye. We are his children, we are his favour, we are his lover, his wife, his bride.
The eagle bearing her young on her wings is still talking about Egypt: “Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself.”

sense.text:
“But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”: we waxed fat, meaning we got wealthy, rich, famous and glorious. “Thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness”: we are now rich. Now it’s jumping from the promised land to the time of Solomon. That was the time we became the greatest, most famous, richest, wealthiest; all nations paid us taxes, and there was no nation to war against.

“Then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation”: that’s Solomon. Notice in verse 15 it is he; in verse 16 it goes from he to they.

precepts.why: Jeshurun waxed fat: “So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom. And all the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart. And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and armour, and spices, horses, and mules”. That is Israel grown thick and covered with fatness.

Then he forsook God which made him. “But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites”, Zidonians and Hittites: so we can’t marry these women, “Of the nations concerning which the Lord said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.” Solomon fell in love when he got up in age.

“And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.” That’s the part. I’ve seen this a lot. Some of you men fall in love, and the woman is here, not because she loves the Lord; she’s just looking at the brothers, what brother could I get. You never question her about the word of God. She might be real pretty, but she ain’t right in the head: she’s on psych meds, she got several baby daddies in the wings waiting, and she’s turning you. A brother that was with us married a beautiful looking sister; where is he today? In the Catholic Church. She pulled his black ashy behind out; that was her goal, that was her mission. And that’s some of you sitting in here.

As a young man, in his prime and his strength, that didn’t happen; they said, we can’t get him, he’s too young, he’s too strong, let’s wait till he gets old and take what he got. “For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.”

“For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians”: write this down, Ashtoreth is Easter; that’s the Canaanite pronunciation, the Canaanite spelling. She’s the goddess of fertility, the one with all the breasts: the worship of a pagan sex goddess. When they say fertility, that means sex, have a lot of babies; that’s where the eggs come from on Easter. “And after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites. And Solomon did evil in the sight of the Lord, and went not fully after the Lord, as did David his father.”

“Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon. And likewise did he for all his strange wives, which burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.” He built false gods for all his strange wives: seven hundred wives, unless a bunch of them worshipped some of the same.

“And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel, which had appeared unto him twice”. This is very important: “I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant. Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father’s sake”: I’m not going to rend the nation of Israel into two kingdoms while you’re alive; I’m going to wait till you’re dead, for David’s sake. “But I will rend it out of the hand of thy son”: I’m going to take it away from your son.

What Solomon’s mama warned him: “Give not thy strength unto women”. Never fall madly in love, making this woman your great I am. Are you stupid? She came from you; she was made for you. Society has twisted it all around. Solomon got old, his understanding started to fail, and his wives turned away his heart.

sense.text: Notice the first word: “They”. Now it goes from he, Solomon, to they. “They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.” This is the history of when the northern kingdom broke off and they started to set up idols, and the Most High got mad with them.
“They sacrificed unto devils, not to God”: that’s what Jeroboam ordained his priests for, “to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not.”
“And when the Lord saw it, he abhorred them”: he hated them, “because of the provoking of his sons, and of his daughters.”

precepts.why:
So now what happened. Remember, God said, I’m not going to rend the kingdom from you, Solomon, for David’s sake, but I’m going to take it from your son, and his son was Rehoboam. “And when all Israel saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to your tents, O Israel”.

“Then king Rehoboam sent Hadoram that was over the tribute; and the children of Israel stoned him with stones, that he died. But king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.” Picture this: he sends an ambassador to call the ten tribes back and they stone him to death, and Rehoboam got in a chariot and got the hell out of there; he said, they’re going to kill me too. “And Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.”

This is what Rehoboam did: “in every several city he put shields and spears, and made them exceeding strong, having Judah and Benjamin on his side.” Judah and Benjamin were the only two tribes there. “And the priests and the Levites that were in all Israel resorted to him out of all their coasts”: the Levites, the priests, left the ten tribes.

Why? “For Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest’s office unto the Lord”. Jeroboam of the tribe of Ephraim became king, and he said, I want all you Levites out. They all got kicked out, so they ran to Judah.

“And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils”: that’s what we were just reading in the song, they sacrificed unto devils, “and for the calves which he had made.” “And after them out of all the tribes of Israel such as set their hearts to seek the Lord God of Israel came to Jerusalem”.

“And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.” That whole thing started and the kingdom got split. Jeroboam became king over the northern kingdom of Israel, kicked out the priests, made other priests of the people, and they started to worship Baal and these images again. That is Israel unmindful of the Rock that begat them, forgetting the God that formed them.

sense.text: “I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.” When it says I will hide my face from them, what happened to our people? We went into slavery: into the Assyrian captivity, the Babylonian captivity, the Persian and Median captivity, the Greek captivity, then the Roman captivity. Our people had no faith.

“They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.” Peter explained this. Moses is going through the history of what would happen, and it did happen, and Paul and Peter expounded on it in their letters. Moses prophesied it, and the captivity Peter and Paul were in was Rome; so we’re reading about Rome.

precepts.why:
This is the people that is not a people. “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light”. Write this down: Peter is quoting Deuteronomy 14:2.

“Which in time past were not a people”: that’s what Moses prophesied in the song when he said I’ll move you to jealousy by them which are not a people. That was the Israelite strangers that were scattered abroad, the northern kingdom. “But are now the people of God”: Christ died and resurrected, and they were being called in, “which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.”

Where Peter got it: “For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.” The chosen generation and peculiar people of 1 Peter 2:9 is Israel, the same people Moses spoke to.

Christians read “Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia” and say, see, all nations, all people, everybody. But read the first word of the next verse: “Elect”. It tells you the elect, the strangers scattered abroad.
Who’s the elect? “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. You Christians better leave us alone with your dumb selves. The elect strangers Peter wrote to are Israel.

Paul quoted it too: “But I say, Did not Israel know? First Moses saith, I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you.” What was Paul telling them? You forgot the song. You forgot the song of Moses. Did not Moses tell you?

sense.text: “For a fire is kindled in mine anger, and shall burn unto the lowest hell”. Verse 21 was the people that are not a people, which Peter and Paul expounded on in the time of Rome; so here we’re reading about Rome.

“I will heap mischiefs upon them; I will spend mine arrows upon them. They shall be burnt with hunger, and devoured with burning heat, and with bitter destruction: I will also send the teeth of beasts upon them”. Y’all remember in the coliseums what they did: they had us fighting all kinds of lions and tigers and bears.
“The sword without, and terror within, shall destroy both the young man and the virgin, the suckling also with the man of gray hairs.”

precepts.why: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far”: Rome, “from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth”: that was their symbol, the eagle. “A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”: they spoke Latin. “A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”: the same as the sword that destroys the young man and the virgin, the suckling and the man of gray hairs.

sense.text: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”.

“Were it not that I feared the wrath of the enemy”: the enemy is Esau. “Lest they should say, Our hand is high, and the Lord hath not done all this”: the white man believes he destroyed us because of his own power. That’s what he thinks in his mind, because the white man really believes he is God.

“For they are a nation void of counsel, neither is there any understanding in them”: talking about us. “O that they were wise, that they understood this, that they would consider their latter end!” Oh that we were wise, that we would understand this, that we would consider our latter end.

“How should one chase a thousand”: how could one man chase a thousand Israelites, “and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them”: except God had sold us, except God was involved and made this to happen. “And the Lord had shut them up”: the Lord is the one that shut us up in captivity.
“For their rock is not as our Rock”: the rock of the nations, their god, is not like our God. “Even our enemies themselves being judges”: our enemies became judges over us.

“For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, and of the fields of Gomorrah: their grapes are grapes of gall, their clusters are bitter”: these are the philosophies we took hold on. He’s still getting on us, because we wanted to be like the other nations.

“Their wine is the poison of dragons, and the cruel venom of asps.” Even if you make the argument and say we were trying to get ourselves together, a lot of us in captivity took hold on the religions of Esau, and those that tried to get right became the people of Sodom and Gomorrah again; our vine became the poison of dragons, the cruel venom of asps. Of course that goes back to Esau, but when we started to take hold of his religions and his politics, it goes for us as well.

precepts.why: I would scatter them into corners: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations”. Those that did not escape were made slaves. Millions escaped down into the coast of Africa, but many got caught and captured. “And Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.”

I would make the remembrance of them to cease: “They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” This is what the nations did to us.

We always read verse 9 on the street, but read 10 as well. “Except the Lord of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.” Watch the next verse: “Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah.” What is he calling the Israelites? Sodom. He’s calling us the people of Gomorrah, because we were wicked as hell. That’s why the song says our vine is of the vine of Sodom and of the fields of Gomorrah.

sense.text: “Is not this laid up in store with me, and sealed up among my treasures?” These are God’s treasures: wisdom, knowledge, the fear of the Lord, which is his word.

“To me belongeth vengeance, and recompence; their foot shall slide in due time”: so we didn’t fully fall a hundred percent. Although we’ve been reading about captivity from the time of Rehoboam all the way up, notice what he says: “for the day of their calamity is at hand, and the things that shall come upon them make haste.” Now he’s going into the 1400s, 1500s, 1600s, 1700s, 1800s, and even before that with the Arabs, the 700s, 800s, 900s, 1000s, with the slave trade.

“For the Lord shall judge his people, and repent himself for his servants, when he seeth that their power is gone, and there is none shut up, or left.” When the Israelites have no more power, there’s none standing for them, none left for them, no prophet, nobody that can stand in righteousness for them. That’s this time period. We were totally, a hundred percent destroyed. At least when Rome destroyed us some of us fled and got away, and you can read books being discovered about the Israelites, how we were conquering and ruling nations; but this time period we have no power.

“And he shall say, Where are their gods, their rock in whom they trusted, Which did eat the fat of their sacrifices, and drank the wine of their drink offerings? let them rise up and help you, and be your protection.” Listen how God is mocking us. Let Allah stand for you. Let Baal stand for you. Let white Jesus stand for you. You want to be a Baptist, let’s see what that does for you; you want to be a Puerto Rican Catholic, let’s see how that stands for you; all this foolishness out here with merry Christmas and all that crap, let’s see how that works. Be your protection: that’s why we’re always marching in the street, no justice, no peace, we shall overcome, with watermelon. The hell is this?

“See now that I, even I, am he, and there is no god with me: I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand.” All the calamities that have befallen us, like we read so often in Deuteronomy 28, are summed up here. This song of Moses gives you the history. He said there’s nobody that can undo what I’ve done to you because of your sins: I’m the one that heals and kills, I’m the one that makes alive.

precepts.why: Sealed up among his treasures: “And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the Lord is his treasure.” Wisdom, knowledge, the fear of the Lord is his treasure, which is his word.

A precept for when their power is gone: “And he shall speak great words against the most High”: that’s the white man blaspheming against the word of God, Sunday morning. “And shall wear out the saints of the most High”: this is how they wore us out, in slavery, in genocide, in destruction, miseducation, lies. The Arabs wore us out too.

“And think to change times and laws”: daylight savings time; he changed the time of the Sabbath; he made the Sabbath on Sunday; he changed Passover to Easter; he turned Hanukkah to Christmas, to keep us in darkness. “And they shall be given into his hand”: the Israelites would be given into this white man’s hand “until a time and times and the dividing of time”, meaning 350 years. That is when the Lord sees that our power is gone.

sense.text: “For I lift up my hand to heaven, and say, I live for ever.” Read it again and see what’s happening there. Now Moses goes into deliverance. Notice when he said he repents himself for his servants “when he seeth that their power is gone, and there is none shut up, or left”: that’s when he begins to wake us up, reawaken us. We’re in that part now. He says, you know what, they’ve had enough; I’m going to send them the Holy Spirit to wake them up, let them see where they have gone wrong.

“If I whet my glittering sword, and mine hand take hold on judgment; I will render vengeance to mine enemies, and will reward them that hate me.” Now he’s telling you, I’m going to deliver y’all, I’m going to save y’all.

“I will make mine arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh”: this is still going into our deliverance. This is destruction. What we’re reading about is missiles flying; destruction is happening, “and that with the blood of the slain and of the captives, from the beginning of revenges upon the enemy.”

precepts.why:
This is the glittering sword. “For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.”

Read on into verse 17: “They that sanctify themselves, and purify themselves in the gardens behind one tree in the midst, eating swine’s flesh, and the abomination, and the mouse, shall be consumed together”. That is who the Lord renders vengeance to when he whets his sword and his hand takes hold on judgment.

“From the beginning of revenges upon the enemy”: “And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?” That’s what our forefathers want: vengeance.

“And white robes were given unto every one of them”: the key is every one of them. Listen to the Bible; this is why y’all need to learn the scriptures. “And it was said unto them, that they should rest yet for a little season, until their fellowservants also and their brethren, that should be killed as they were, should be fulfilled.”

When we think about under the altar, we think small. We have to think big about what’s going on up there: these souls are walking around and talking with the Lord. You think of an altar and you think of a little square box with the Lord looking in it; it’s not that. The Lord is telling the apostles and those prophets, just wait a little while: there are more prophets that have to die.

The blood of the slain: “And in her was found the blood of prophets”, because America is going to kill the prophets. That hasn’t happened yet, but it’s going to. “And of saints”: that’s men and women too, “and of all that were slain upon the earth.” That is the blood the Lord avenges when he makes his arrows drunk with blood.

sense.text: Moses’ song just said he will avenge the blood of his servants and will render vengeance to his adversaries. Christ in Luke 18 is saying the same thing the song of Moses said. “That men ought always to pray, and not to faint”: don’t give up praying. That’s what he’s saying, don’t give up.
“There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man”: this is the Lord.
“And there was a widow in that city”: this widow represents Israel. “And she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.” We just read in Lamentations that the adversaries were the nations.

“And he would not for a while”: he hid his face from us, like we read in Deuteronomy, in the song. “But afterward he said within himself”: this is what we just read in Deuteronomy 32, then shall the Lord repent himself when he seeth that their power is gone and there is none shut up or left.
“Yet because this widow troubleth me”: she troubles him with asking, praying day after day. “I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me.”
He breaks it down: “And shall not God avenge his own elect”: the elect are the Israelites, “which cry day and night unto him”, which pray day and night unto him, “though he bear long with them?”
“I tell you that he will avenge them speedily.” Y’all see that right there. “Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?”

precepts.why:
Who is the widow? “Fear not; for thou shalt not be ashamed: neither be thou confounded; for thou shalt not be put to shame: for thou shalt forget the shame of thy youth, and shalt not remember the reproach of thy widowhood any more.”

Read on: “For thy Maker is thine husband; the Lord of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called.” So this widow is of the Holy One of Israel: it’s Israel. The widow is Israel.

Another one for the widow, a better one. “How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people! how is she become as a widow!” See that: how is she become as a widow. “She that was great among the nations”: we were great among the nations, “and princess among the provinces, how is she become tributary!”

“She weepeth sore in the night, and her tears are on her cheeks: among all her lovers she hath none to comfort her: all her friends have dealt treacherously with her, they are become her enemies. Judah is gone into captivity because of affliction, and because of great servitude: she dwelleth among the heathen, she findeth no rest: all her persecutors overtook her between the straits.”

“The ways of Zion do mourn, because none come to the solemn feasts”: nobody was keeping the Passover, nobody wanted to keep the Sabbath day, nobody wanted to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, nobody wanted to keep the memorial of blowing of trumpets, so forth and so on. “All her gates are desolate: her priests sigh, her virgins are afflicted, and she is in bitterness.” Watch this: “Her adversaries are the chief, her enemies prosper; for the Lord hath afflicted her for the multitude of her transgressions: her children are gone into captivity before the enemy.”

Go back to verse 1 so we don’t forget the thought: “how is she become as a widow!” That’s the point. The widow in Luke 18 is Israel, and the adversaries she asks to be avenged of are the nations.

sense.text:
“Rejoice, O ye nations, with his people”: after they get subdued, they better rejoice, and they’re going to. They’re going to bow the knee to the King of Kings; that’s what he’s talking about. “For he will avenge the blood of his servants, and will render vengeance to his adversaries”.

“And will be merciful unto his land, and to his people”: so the mercy is only going to be on our land and on our people. It’s not for all nations. The other nations that are going to be made to rejoice, they’re going to be in captivity.
“And Moses came and spake all the words of this song in the ears of the people, he, and Hoshea the son of Nun.” Hoshea is Joshua; that’s who Hoshea is.

“And he said, The Lord came from Sinai”: he sees a vision. “And rose up from Seir unto them”: that’s Edom. He rose up from the land of Edom, because that’s where the destruction is going to be. “He shined forth from mount Paran, and he came with ten thousands of saints”.

“From his right hand went a fiery law for them”: the images are depictions of that. He’s going to teach Israel while we’re in the wilderness. He’s going to give us the history all over again and teach us all over again, and any rebel that’s there: off with your head.
“Yea, he loved the people; all his saints are in thy hand: and they sat down at thy feet; every one shall receive of thy words.” See that: everybody is going to receive of thy words.

“Open ye the gates, that the righteous nation which keepeth the truth may enter in.” That’s some heavy stuff. Open ye the gates: what gates? The gates to the 12 tribes of Israel. So only Israelites enter in these gates; the other nations are not getting in.

“Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee”: that’s for all of you men and women who have psychological hiccups. Meditate on verse 3. You want a peaceful mentality, keep your mind on the scriptures. Stop going out, stop watching them damn shows with them whorish women always fist fighting, Basketball Wives and Love and Hip Hop, all that foolishness. Then you think, oh, that’s how I got to act with my man. No, you all jacked up in the head. Stop it. “Because he trusteth in thee.”

“Trust ye in the Lord for ever: for in the Lord Jehovah is everlasting strength”. See how they have Jehovah spelled with three syllables, J-E, H-O, V-A-H. As we know, there was no J in Hebrew, neither was there a V: for the J you can write Y, and for the V put a W.

“For he bringeth down them that dwell on high; the lofty city, he layeth it low”: he’s going to lay down the lofty city. That’s America; he’s going to destroy it, “even to the ground”, “even to the dust.”
“The foot shall tread it down, even the feet of the poor”: that’s us, “and the steps of the needy”: by us teaching the word, going here and there.

“Yea, in the way of thy judgments, O Lord, have we waited for thee; the desire of our soul is to thy name, and to the remembrance of thee.” The desire of our soul is to thy name and to the remembrance of thee: that’s the Bible, the Holy Bible. That’s what it’s making reference to.

“With my soul have I desired thee in the night”: in the night we have to send up our prayers to the Lord. “Yea, with my spirit within me will I seek thee early: for when thy judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness.”

This is why we pray for judgments to come into the earth. We’re praying for the Lord to bring the storm, the wind, the earthquakes, the fires, the flame, even the terrorism. We are praying for the Lord’s judgments to be seen, so that all the world will know that he is our God and none else.

Pay attention to verse 10. “Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness: in the land of uprightness”: that’s the land of Israel, “will he deal unjustly”. Do we not see him dealing unjustly with the Palestinians? “And will not behold the majesty of the Lord”: they don’t know the Lord, with their HaShem and all that crap. They don’t know; they’re the most evil, wicked people on the earth.

“Lord, when thy hand is lifted up, they will not see”: they ain’t going to see the Lord’s hand lifted up. “But they shall see”: they don’t want to see when we’re prophesying, but they’re going to see when it comes to pass. “And be ashamed for their envy at the people”: they’re envious of us. They took our land, they took our identity; they’re going to be ashamed.

“Yea, the fire of thine enemies shall devour them”: you’re going to get destroyed.
“Lord, thou wilt ordain peace for us”: God will ordain peace for us, “for thou also hast wrought all our works in us.”

“O Lord our God, other lords beside thee have had dominion over us”: meaning all races, all nations had us in captivity. “But by thee only will we make mention of thy name”: we’re only going to pray to the one true God.

“They are dead, they shall not live”: these nations are dead and they shall not live again. “They are deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them”: that’s why he’s going to come back with vengeance, “and made all their memory to perish.” God’s going to wipe out all their memory. There ain’t going to be no ‘what about the white man?’ To hell with him; who is that? I don’t know who that is. That’s a heavy verse; that verse right there gives me chills.

“Lord, in trouble have they visited thee, they poured out a prayer when thy chastening was upon them”: that’s what we’re doing. As we’re being chastised, we’re sending out our prayers to the Lord for mercy and forgiveness.

“Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs; so have we been in thy sight, O Lord.” The Lord sees us as his bride, a pregnant woman. That’s how he’s looking at us, crying out.

“We have been with child, we have been in pain, we have as it were brought forth wind; we have not wrought any deliverance in the earth; neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen.” We’re waiting for the nations to fall, but they have not fallen yet.

“Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise.” This verse right here is very heavy. “Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead.” See that: the earth shall cast out the dead.

“Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers”: this is talking about the chariots, and there’s some Israelites that don’t believe this. “And shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment”: why? “Until the indignation be overpast”: meaning until the destruction is over. Hide yourself in your chambers, the chariots, until the destruction is passed. When that destruction comes, that’s going to be in the time of deliverance.

“For, behold, the Lord cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.” That’s the proof: total destruction is coming, and the Lord is going to deliver the elect that keep his laws.

precepts.why: The gates: the city “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels”. It’s going to be 12 big black angels at the gates, “and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”. Those are the gates Isaiah says to open for the righteous nation.

The precept to prove what thy name is: “And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.”

This needs to be stressed, because you’ve got men that always say, oh no, you just got to meditate on the name. But meanwhile the book is closed; they won’t do one law, one statute, one judgment that’s in it. That’s not his name, sir. What you’re doing is foolishness, evil, sin. His name is the word of God, so when the desire of our soul is to thy name, it is to the Holy Bible.

They’re going to be ashamed for their envy at us; they want to be us so bad. “The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee”. See what the word of God says: they ain’t going to be able to do nothing against us.

“Together with my dead body shall they arise”: “Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days? But he spake of the temple of his body.”

He said destroy this temple and I’ll raise it up in three days. Watch it with what we just read in Isaiah 26:19: thy dead men shall live, together with his dead body shall they arise, in three days.

He said in three days. “Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn”: he tore us in captivity, “and he will heal us”: he will revive us. “He hath smitten, and he will bind us up”: he’s going to bind us back to 12 tribes again.

Watch this: “After two days will he revive us”. If two days are past, what day would it be? The third. So we’re being revived. “In the third day”: that’s the day we’re living in right now, “he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight.” That is the rising of the dead men of Isaiah 26:19, together with his dead body.

The earth shall cast out the dead: “For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.” The dead in Christ shall rise first.

“And those that be dead will I raise up again from their places, and bring them out of the graves: for I have known my name in Israel.” So we should never worry about death. That is what Isaiah means: the earth shall cast out the dead.

Here’s the precept for the chambers: “And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud”. Like I said, the cloud there is the chariot. Some Israelites don’t believe that; they make mockery of this. Keep on making jokes. “And their enemies beheld them.”

“And the same hour”, meaning the same time, “was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell”: total destruction, “and in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand”: everybody dead. That is the indignation Isaiah says to hide from in your chambers until it is overpast.

This is what it’s all about. A brother said, no, we’ve all got to go to Egypt or South Africa and hide there; don’t believe those scriptures about being delivered up by chariots or clouds, and he started laughing. Okay, the joke is going to be on you. All these that claim to be Israelites do not believe everything that’s in the Bible.

“He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler. Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day; Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday.” He tells you when the destruction is going to happen: at noonday.

“A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand”: the message to the elect of Israel is that you’re going to see a thousand dead bodies burnt and disintegrated at one side and ten thousand on the other, “but it shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.” Why? “Because thou hast made the Lord, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation”.

That’s what Revelation was saying, and Isaiah 26:20 is saying the same thing: hide thyself for a little moment until the indignation be overpast.

sense.text: “And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion”: the Lamb is Christ, standing on Mount Zion with the Israelites. “And with him an hundred forty and four thousand”: the leaders of Israel standing with Christ, “having his Father’s name written in their foreheads”, because Christ is going to give us the true name of the Father that’s been hidden forever.

“These are they which were not defiled with women”: they’re not going to give their strength to women, like we read in Proverbs: don’t give your strength to women. You ought to serve the one true God and follow him; she is to follow us, not the other way around. Some of y’all got it twisted: soon as she opens her legs you follow it all up in there. No, follow the one true God.

precepts.why:
What is this new song? “And they sung a new song, saying, Thou art worthy to take the book, and to open the seals thereof”: this new song is the song of the Lamb. “For thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood”: he died on the cross for us and redeemed us.

“Out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation”: those are the key words to stress when you teach. These are the Israelites coming out from nation and nation and peoples and tongues.

“And hast made us unto our God kings and priests”: we’re going to be a nation of kings and priests, “and we shall reign on the earth.”

sense.text: This song of the Lamb is heavy: we’re going to reign with Christ as kings and priests. “Praise ye the Lord. Sing unto the Lord a new song”: a what song? A new song. This is the same new song we read about in Revelation; this is the song of the Lamb. “And his praise in the congregation of saints.”

“Let Israel rejoice in him that made him”: why is he saying it like that? Because our people have not been rejoicing in him that made us. We’ve been rejoicing in the white man: Thanksgiving, Easter, Halloween. “Let the children of Zion be joyful in their King”: we’ve got to be joyful in our King.

“For the Lord taketh pleasure in his people”: on the street, you want to stress that. He don’t take pleasure in everybody on the planet; he takes pleasure in his people. “He will beautify the meek with salvation”: he’s going to beautify us once again.
“Let the saints be joyful in glory: let them sing aloud upon their beds”, because we’re going to be in righteousness in the kingdom of heaven.
“Let the high praises of God be in their mouth, and a twoedged sword in their hand”: see the picture; this is what the Bible is talking about. The word of God in our mouth is the Bible.
What are we going to do? “To execute vengeance upon the heathen”: we’re going to execute vengeance upon the nations, “and punishments upon the people”: upon all the peoples of the earth.
“To bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron”: we’re going to bind their kings in chains. Just like they did to us, we’re going to do to them.
“To execute upon them the judgment written”: whatever this Bible says, we’re going to execute it upon them. “This honour have all his saints. Praise ye the Lord.”
